sources.title: Haile Gebrselassie (Q171500) -- verified live via the Wikidata API (2026-10-24): English label 'Haile Gebrselassie', description 'Ethiopian long-distance runner and businessman (born 1973)', Korean label '하일레 게브르셀라시에', born 18 April 1973, no death date, citizenship Ethiopia. Orientation only; not used as support for any row. (The hinted item Q312044 is a reptile species and was not used.)

Rolf Bryhn, 'Haile Gebrselassie', Store norske leksikon (Norwegian national encyclopedia, updated November 2024; read in full in Norwegian): Olympic 10,000 metres champion at Atlanta 1996 and Sydney 2000, world champion in 1993, 1995, 1997 and 1999, fifth at Athens 2004 and sixth at Beijing 2008, the switch to road racing after 2004, marathon wins at Amsterdam, Berlin (2006-2009), Fukuoka and Dubai, 27 official and unofficial world records from 2000 metres to the marathon, the 2:03:59 Berlin marathon record that stood until September 2011, the IAAF's 1998 male athlete award, and the November 2010 New York Marathon withdrawal and retirement announcement. CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE. Reference-work entry by an outside author; no trait claims.

Chris Chavez, 'Even in retirement, Haile Gebrselassie is still running strong', Sports Illustrated, 30 October 2015 (read in full): his May 2015 retirement after the Great Manchester Run, his 2010 New York Marathon exit followed by a declaration he was stopping, his return to competition the next April with only one more marathon completed, 27 world records and 11 major marathon wins, the 2007 and 2008 Berlin marathon records (2:04:26 and 2:03:59), his Hall of Fame induction, his current twice-a-day running, and his own remarks on Mo Farah and Eliud Kipchoge. Sports-magazine interview report; much of the colour is his own words (self-account), the career facts are the writer's. Family and illness passages were not used.

Simon Robinson, 'Quotes of the Day: the traditional clash between Ethiopia and Kenya in distance running', TIME, 8 August 2004 (read in full): Kenenisa Bekele inspired by Gebrselassie; Ethiopia's centrally controlled system under coach Woldemeskel Kostre versus Kenya's free-market approach; an account of the coach telling Gebrselassie before the Sydney Games that he could not be put in the team unless he travelled with it, after which he came and won; Kenyan and Ethiopian officials' contrasting remarks; the writer's note that Gebrselassie owns well-known Addis Ababa property (business, not scored). Independent magazine feature with Kenyan, Ethiopian and British voices; medical details in the Sydney episode were not used.

AthleticsAfrica, 'Haile Gebrselassie' profile (last updated 2005, read in full): the Arsi origins of Ethiopian distance runners, his 1992 world junior titles, first world record at 5000 metres in 1994, the 1996 Atlanta 10,000 metres in which he tracked Paul Tergat and won by six metres, and the 2000 Sydney final in which he edged Tergat 'in the very last stride'. Athletics-website profile with some admiring wording and a childhood anecdote that was not used; read for the race accounts.

AthleticsAfrica, 'Ethiopian Gebrselassie quits running after New York heartbreak', 8 November 2010 (read in full): the retirement announcement after he dropped out of the 2010 New York City Marathon, the abandoned plan to win a third Olympic gold in London 2012, his 18-year international career with two Olympic golds, eight world titles and 27 world records, and his words 'let me give a chance to the youngsters'. Short news report quoting him; the injury detail was not used, and the later reversal is taken from the Sports Illustrated report.

Daily Nation (Kenya), 'Plot to put Ethiopians in their place', 23 July 2009 (read in full): Kenyan runners' stated plans to beat Bekele and Gebrselassie at the Berlin World Championships, including a Kenyan runner beaten by Gebrselassie in the final kick at Hengelo who wanted revenge. Rival-side press report used only as a counter-voice on his place as a benchmark opponent; no behavioural row rests on it alone.

Wikimedia Commons file page 'Olympic great Haile Gebrselassie speaking at the Olympic hunger summit in Downing Street, 12 August 2012 (cropped).jpg' and the Flickr photo page of the UK Foreign and Commonwealth Office (live check 2026-10-24) -- checked for the portrait: photograph by the Foreign and Commonwealth Office, taken 12 August 2012.

competitiveness.rationale: [src_hg_athafrica, src_hg_snl, src_hg_nation | 1996-2009 | athletics profile + encyclopedia + rival-side press] The profile describes the Atlanta 10,000 metres in which he tracked Tergat and surged to win by six metres and the Sydney final decided in the last stride; the encyclopedia lists two Olympic titles and four world titles; the Kenyan paper shows rivals still targeting him in 2009. Repeated wins in close finishes against a named rival are documented, but the race narratives come from one profile and no source describes his attitude to competing, hence a moderate-high confidence.

persistence.rationale: [src_hg_snl, src_hg_si, src_hg_athafrica2010 | 1992-2015 | encyclopedia + magazine + news report] The encyclopedia gives an elite career from the early 1990s, with Olympic participation at Athens 2004 and Beijing 2008 and marathon wins through 2010; the news report says he announced retirement in November 2010 and the magazine says he returned the next April, with a final retirement in 2015 after the Great Manchester Run. Longevity and a refusal to stop at the first announced ending are documented; his own words about running every day are self-account, so a moderate confidence.

adaptability.rationale: [src_hg_snl, src_hg_si | 2004-2009 | encyclopedia + magazine] After finishing fifth in the Athens 10,000 metres he moved his main effort to road racing, winning the Berlin Marathon four years running and setting marathon world records in 2007 and 2008 (2:04:26 and 2:03:59). A change of event with a documented outcome from two independent writers; the reasons are not stated in either, so a moderate confidence.

achievement_drive.rationale: [src_hg_snl, src_hg_athafrica2010, src_hg_si | 1992-2012 | encyclopedia + news report + magazine] The encyclopedia and magazine count 27 world records across distances from 2000 metres to the marathon; the 2010 news report says his plan was to win a third Olympic gold at London 2012. Sustained pursuit of records across many events is documented, while the goal is stated in one short news item, so a moderate confidence.

discipline.rationale: [src_hg_time, src_hg_si | 2000-2015 | magazine feature + magazine interview] TIME records the Ethiopian coach telling him before Sydney that he had to travel with the team or be left out, after which he joined it and won; the interview says he still trains twice a day in retirement. One episode told through the coach and a self-reported routine, hence a modest score at low confidence. SELF-CALIBRATION (agent): first-pass 62 / 0.5 lowered to 54 / 0.4 because the Sydney episode rests on one coach's account and the routine is his own statement.

portrait.source: Wikimedia Commons, 'Olympic great Haile Gebrselassie speaking at the Olympic hunger summit in Downing Street, 12 August 2012 (cropped).jpg' -- photograph of Haile Gebrselassie published by the UK Foreign and Commonwealth Office on its Flickr stream (photo 7766483966), taken 12 August 2012. The live Flickr photo page (2026-10-24) shows the photo itself under CC BY 2.0 with owner 'foreignoffice'; the Commons page tags it OGL v1.0 on the basis of the FCO stream. Both licences allow reuse with attribution; the photo-level CC BY 2.0 on Flickr is the licence recorded here. Commons crop 1235 x 1387 pixels from a 2128 x 1416 original; stored file downscaled to 1068 x 1200, never upscaled. CAVEAT FOR THE LEAD: the photo-level licence (CC BY 2.0) differs from the Commons licence tag (OGL v1.0); the Flickr photo page lists no OGL statement. If the strict rule against any licence mismatch applies, set this portrait to held; the next step would be a different file with a single consistent licence (the other candidates on Commons are uploader-assertion own-work photos or lower-quality). Alternatives rejected: the 2010 Manchester Run file (own-work, poor-quality side shot), a 2010 Dubai file tagged public domain by the uploader without basis, and photographs taken with other people.

provenance.notes: PREFLIGHT: QID VERIFIED LIVE: Wikidata wbgetentities (2026-10-24) for Q171500 returned en label 'Haile Gebrselassie', description 'Ethiopian long-distance runner and businessman (born 1973)', ko label '하일레 게브르셀라시에', born 1973-04-18, no death date, citizenship Ethiopia. SLUG/QID CHECK: no data-pipeline candidate or src file for slug haile-gebrselassie or QID Q171500 (haile-selassie is a different person). REGION: sub_saharan_africa. VOCABULARY: occupation athlete, field sport, tags competitor and sustained_excellence, archetype competitive_performer are existing labelled ids. ZERO POLITICS: his 2012 appearance at a Downing Street summit is only the setting of the portrait; no political, advocacy or governmental activity is scored. LIVING SUBJECT: public documented sporting conduct only. Excluded: his later business activities (the writer's mention of Addis Ababa property is not scored), family and bereavement (an eldest sister's death in the SI piece was read and not used), injuries and medical reasons for withdrawals (the 2010 knee problem and a medical detail in the Sydney anecdote were deliberately left out), the Beijing 2008 marathon decision, rumours, any politics. PORTRAIT PREFLIGHT: FCO photograph with a licence mismatch between Flickr (CC BY 2.0) and Commons (OGL v1.0), recorded in portrait.source for the lead. CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: Rolf Bryhn, Store norske leksikon entry (https://snl.no/Haile_Gebrselassie; read in full in Norwegian). READ (7 cited non-Wikidata sources): Store norske leksikon, Sports Illustrated, TIME, AthleticsAfrica profile, AthleticsAfrica 2010 news report, Daily Nation, plus the Commons and Flickr pages for the portrait. Not opened or blocked: Olympics.com and World Athletics athlete pages (script-rendered, nothing readable), Washington Times AP piece on Bekele's marathon (empty on fetch), LetsRun (empty), books and magazine features by others. PERSPECTIVES: reference encyclopedia (SNL), US sports magazine (SI), international news magazine with Kenyan and Ethiopian voices (TIME), Ethiopian-/African athletics sites, and Kenyan national press (rival side). The SI interview is partly self-account. Independent behavioural support: SNL, TIME and AthleticsAfrica race accounts. COUNTER-VOICES (thin): Kenyan runners and officials in TIME and the Daily Nation present him as an opponent to beat and TIME describes the tight state control under which Ethiopian runners worked; no source read criticises his professional conduct, so the profile makes no claim about how he treated rivals or federation officials. Rivalry with Bekele is only evidenced as Bekele being inspired by him (TIME), not as a documented contest, and is unscored. SELF-CALIBRATION: reviewed discipline (lowered, see row), competitiveness (kept at 76 / 0.62: two Olympic finishes with a named rival are independently listed and confidence is already moderate) and persistence (kept at 72 / 0.58: dates are documented, only the daily-routine quote is self-reported). No row on collaboration, risk tolerance or leadership because the sources do not document them. PORTRAIT: see portrait.source.
